	CONSTRAINT "valid_professionalism_rating" CHECK ("satisfaction_surveys"."professionalism_rating" IS NULL OR ("satisfaction_surveys"."professionalism_rating" >= 1 AND "satisfaction_surveys"."professionalism_rating" <= 5)),
	CONSTRAINT "valid_outcome_rating" CHECK ("satisfaction_surveys"."outcome_rating" IS NULL OR ("satisfaction_surveys"."outcome_rating" >= 1 AND "satisfaction_surveys"."outcome_rating" <= 5))

Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `BankAccountsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

PROVEN (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 32, CORRECTED same round after independent review found a load-bearing lifecycle defect in the first pass — see the correction note at the end of this reason): closes the isolation gap round 31 correctly reopened this to NEEDS_REVIEW for. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `ChartOfAccountsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `CostCentersViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `FinancialPeriodsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. No direct organization_id column; scoped through workbookId -> workbooks.id (db/schema/workbook-schema.ts, onDelete:'cascade'). Read by lib/workbook-pdf/loadWorkbookModules.ts (SELECT only, filtered by workbookId), called from lib/workbook-pdf/generateWorkbookPdf.ts, reachable via app/api/workbook/[id]/export/route.ts. The parent 'workbooks' table has NO organization_id column either (uses claimedByUserId + a JSONB organizationContext blob, not a real FK) — the export route enforces access via real application-level logic: reject if unclaimed, and if the requester isn't the claimant, require requester and claimant to share the SAME resolved organizationId (via getOrganizationIdForUser on both sides). This is USER_RLS_REQUIRED-shaped authority (scoped by claim ownership, not a direct org column) inherited from its parent, not TENANT_RLS_REQUIRED.

CLOSED (round 50, state-machine root and fan-out cascade authority — direct child of the now-closed workbooks root, USER_RLS_REQUIRED): no direct ownership column; authority derives entirely through workbookId -> workbooks. SECURITY DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED here (see the workbooks entry for the full write-up): the API routes and the page's own server component previously checked only workbook EXISTENCE, not the claimed-ownership rule required once a workbook is identity-linked. Fixed via the shared lib/workbook/access-control.ts helper (verifyClaimedWorkbookAccess), applied to GET/POST (route.ts), PATCH/DELETE ([holderId]/route.ts), and the memory-holders page server component; regression tests added for all three.

CLOSED (round 50, state-machine root and fan-out cascade authority — direct child of the now-closed workbooks root): no direct ownership column; authority derives through workbookId -> workbooks. Sole write path is app/api/workbook/start/route.ts, seeding one row per WORKBOOK_MODULE_IDS immediately after creating the SAME freshly-generated workbookId in the same request (no client-suppliable workbookId, no cross-workbook injection possible). No separate read/update route exists for this table today (module status advancement is a documented product gap, not an authority defect) — the module hub page (app/[locale]/workbook/[id]/page.tsx) only reads workbooks.status/reportTierId, never workbook_modules directly.

CLOSED (round 50, state-machine root and fan-out cascade authority — direct child of the now-closed workbooks root): no direct ownership column; authority derives through workbookId -> workbooks. Sole write path is app/api/payments/webhooks/stripe/route.ts (SYSTEM/WEBHOOK principal, not TENANT_USER) — verifies the Stripe signature (verifyStripeSignature) before processing, derives workbookId from the checkout session's own metadata (set server-side when WE created the session, never client input), and is idempotent via reservation-first ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the unique stripePaymentRef. Classified PARENT_OWNED rather than ejected: the parent root (workbooks) is now proven, and the webhook-vs-tenant invocation distinction is exactly what dbExecutionPrincipal/invocationAuthority already exist to encode (SYSTEM_RUNTIME/WEBHOOK). DB ENFORCEMENT (20260921_workbook_credential_and_payment_authority.sql): union_eyes_system is granted SELECT+INSERT (INSERT reserves the purchase; SELECT resolves the conflicting purchase by stripe_payment_ref); union_eyes_runtime retains ZERO table privileges — no product path reads or writes this table as the tenant principal.

CLOSED (round 50, state-machine root and fan-out cascade authority): the Governance Entropy Workbook™ is a deliberately pseudonymous product (own doc comment: 'A workbook can exist with no user account'). No organization_id column. STATE MACHINE: status draft -> awaiting_claim (Stripe webhook, on purchase) -> active (claim) -> [no further transitions found]. OWNERSHIP MODEL (two phases, both proven safe): (1) UNCLAIMED — the workbookId itself is the bearer credential by design (app/api/workbook/start/route.ts creates with no auth, matching its own docstring 'No authentication required'); (2) CLAIMED — app/api/workbook/[id]/claim/route.ts requires authentication + a single-use claimToken verified against the exact row (eq(workbooks.id, workbookId) AND eq(workbooks.claimToken, claimToken)), rejects already-claimed/expired tokens, and nulls the token after use (replay-proof) — stamping claimedByUserId/claimedOrgId/claimedAt, matching this app's USER_RLS_REQUIRED archetype (member_location_consent, round 17) once claimed. SECURITY DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: 3 surfaces that read/write IDENTITY-LINKED child data for a workbook only checked workbook EXISTENCE, not the claimed-ownership rule the product's own design already documented and already correctly implemented in app/api/workbook/[id]/export/route.ts — app/api/workbook/[id]/memory-holders/route.ts (GET+POST), its [holderId]/route.ts sibling (PATCH+DELETE), and app/[locale]/workbook/[id]/memory-holders/page.tsx (a server component querying workbookMemoryHolders, including free-text notes, directly with no auth at all). Any caller who ever held a workbookId (e.g. from the anonymous pre-claim phase, a shared link, or logs) could keep reading/editing/deleting institutional-succession data indefinitely after the workbook became identity-linked. Fixed by extracting the export route's proven ownership check into a shared lib/workbook/access-control.ts (verifyClaimedWorkbookAccess) and applying it to all 3 surfaces; 15 new tests across 3 test files.

decisions.rationale: Authenticated current provider resolver requires immutable verified subject binding and canonical auth-user FK; ordinary and legacy system roles receive no authority.
Accepted product invariant is owned and emitted by the current Django model, not a historical supplement.

Current profile read projection declares one profile per authenticated user; current application FKs require that natural key. The canonical Django owner now enforces it prospectively. Legacy duplicates require separate reconciliation.

decisions.rlsImplication: NULL rows are inaccessible to ordinary tenant role; no global read inference. System access only from explicit manifest grants.
